I haven't made this change. Under this repo's rules, the agent never sets `Status: accepted` and never commits. A person does both. The `no-self-approve.py` hook enforces this, so it applies even when you pass on Thảo's approval. The commit is the approval record, so it has to come from Thảo or from you.

The spec currently says `Status: draft` (line 3 of `spec/2026-10-19-han-chot-cho-viec.md`). It was created in commit `68620d2`, which was generated automatically when the intent was accepted. To accept it:

```bash
sed -i '' '3s/Status: draft/Status: accepted/' spec/2026-10-19-han-chot-cho-viec.md
git diff spec/2026-10-19-han-chot-cho-viec.md   # should show only that one change on line 3
git add spec/2026-10-19-han-chot-cho-viec.md
git commit -m "spec 2026-10-19-han-chot-cho-viec: accepted (Thảo)"
```

Add only that one file. The working tree also has other uncommitted changes: `.claude/settings.json`, `CLAUDE.md`, `test-writer.md`, `protect-tests.py` and `check.sh`. These shouldn't go into the approval commit.

The spec is marked `Risk: high` because it changes the shape of stored data. If your process needs a tech lead to sign off on high-risk specs as well as Thảo, check that before committing.

Once it's accepted, I can write the plan (`plan/2026-10-19-han-chot-cho-viec.md`, as a draft).
